title: Watertown Cancelling Contract for Flock License Plate Reading Cameras
summary: Watertown, MA City Manager George Proakis announced the city is canceling its contract with Flock Safety for eight license plate reader cameras, none of which had been installed. The decision followed ACLU of Massachusetts concerns about Flock sharing data with out-of-state and federal agencies, and resident pushback at a Jan. 21 Tech Talk over potential use by federal immigration enforcement.

key_quotes.quote: While I have a lot of faith in how our Police manages their policies and their data, I can't sit here and vouch for some outside company on this level, and I don't want to do that under these circumstances
The ACLU of Massachusetts contacted Watertown and other communities about Flock sharing information with law enforcement outside the state, and at the federal level.
Most of the residents there expressed concerns about the Flock cameras and that the data collected could be used by federal immigration enforcement agencies.
